findings.location: §5 B3; §8.1 rows for r2 §3 PR5 and §4 release; §11 R4-02
findings.claim: Partially closed. The new table restores many requirements, but still drops the protected release ref/tag and exact-H required CI checks from r2 §4 Release. B3 checks a clean H/package and a full-audit receipt; neither proves H is an authorized release revision or has passed the other required CI checks. The table maps only candidate/definition identity and component exceptions, without retaining or explicitly rejecting these two requirements. The r2 dashboard requirement to show current master versus the audited snapshot also has no explicit destination.

evidence.observed: r2 §4 requires H/tree plus a protected tag/ref, required CI checks on H, and current-master/audited-H drift display.
B3 and the trace rows contain no protected-ref or required-CI predicate; B2 records snapshot age without the requested master drift display.

The actual checkout is 0 commits behind origin/master and 2 ahead. Thus the existing PowerShell not-behind check accepts an unmerged revision; it is not a protected-ref membership check. The shell deploy script has no equivalent remote CI check.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore these source obligations explicitly in B3/B2 and §8, or give an explicit owner-approved rejection and rationale. B3 should resolve the authorized protected release ref, bind it to H/tree/package, and verify all required CI contexts on the correct provenance before push. Test a clean ahead-of-master candidate with a successful audit but a failed/missing required CI check, and a moved release ref. Keep waivers separate; do not confuse not-behind with authorized-for-release or turn unknown API results into pass.

findings.claim: Partially closed. Six-hour polling, readback, heartbeat and an explicitly best-effort deadline fix the original timing overclaim. The replacement failure path still incorrectly asserts that a failed scheduled watchdog automatically notifies the repository owner. GitHub notification routing depends on the workflow/cron actor and notification settings. If Issue writes fail, the claimed fallback recipient is therefore unproved.

evidence.observed: Line 117 says GitHub reports the failed scheduled run to the owner; no recipient/subscription verification is specified.

Scheduled notifications follow the workflow creator, a later cron editor, or the re-enabling user; delivery also depends on enabled notification settings. Owner status alone does not select the recipient. [GitHub notification contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/notifications-for-workflow-runs).

findings.suggested_fix: Make notification ownership/subscription and a verified fallback delivery path part of B2 activation, or mark delivery unmeasured and rely on an explicitly assigned external observer. Test failed Issue writes and a missing watchdog with the intended recipient. Retain the best-effort qualification; merely making the Actions job red must not be reported as owner notification delivered.

findings.claim: Partially closed. The trusted merge-side consumer and invalidation of previously green targeted evidence are sound improvements. However, collaborator/role enumeration does not establish the complete variable-writer set: GitHub App installation credentials can also have Variables:write. Moreover, the same write permission permits both disabling and re-enabling, while Q9 reserves re-enabling to the owner. Reading an allowed string and a collaborator list does not demonstrate that the owner authorized the current enable transition.

evidence.observed: A+1 specifies REST collaborator/role measurement and string-based enablement; Q9 permits delegated switch-off but owner-only switch-on. No enable-transition authority record or App-writer disposition is specified.

Repository variable updates support App installation tokens with Variables:write. The update endpoint accepts a value without an off-only permission, and the read response supplies value/timestamps, not the author of the current value. [GitHub variable API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/variables#update-a-repository-variable).

findings.suggested_fix: Have Q9 decide the complete principal/credential scope, including Apps, and distinguish procedural trust from machine enforcement. Either constrain actual writers appropriately or require a durable owner-authorized activation generation which the trusted consumer validates; delegated disablement must invalidate old activation evidence. Test an App writer and an off-authorized operator attempting to re-enable. Unknown writer coverage must require full execution. No variable or credential changes are authorized by this review.

findings.claim: The new seventh activation condition calls a before/after cohort difference instrumentation overhead. Even with day_du/success filtering and PR clustering, product changes, mutant inventory and runner load can change G5 duration. This can approve instrumentation whose real overhead exceeds 5%, or remove acceptable instrumentation. Clustering estimates dependence; it does not provide the missing counterfactual.

evidence.observed: Executed deterministic witness: before=100 s; after underlying work=75 s plus 20% instrumentation gives 90 s. The plan reports -10% and passes the 5% threshold despite true overhead=20%. Conversely underlying work=120 s and zero instrumentation overhead reports +20% and fails. Repetition within PR clusters preserves both errors.
A+5 uses pre/post PR1 merge step durations from the 14-day shadow cohort, without paired instrumentation-on/off measurements on identical inputs.

findings.suggested_fix: Use paired on/off measurements on the same immutable product/test/mutant snapshot and environment, with repeated/interleaved runs and a declared estimator. Keep the 14-day cohort as operational monitoring. Assign the measurement to a successor or future PR3 prerequisite without changing frozen PR1. Add the two confounding witnesses and positive controlled-overhead cases to the measurement acceptance; do not claim synthetic examples are production timings.

findings.claim: The B3 fallback says to invoke A4 for the release run when definition identity is not_measured, but its deployment capability contract only requires Actions-read. ops-do-workflow-definition.yml is workflow_dispatch-only. Its internal read-only permissions do not grant a caller permission to start it. The advertised fallback is therefore unavailable to a minimally provisioned deploy host; silently obtaining write credentials would also expand the authority boundary.

evidence.observed: The existing A4 workflow has only workflow_dispatch with run_id input. Its job has contents:read/actions:read; these are execution permissions, not dispatch authorization.
A fine-grained caller token needs Actions:write to create the dispatch event. [GitHub dispatch permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event).
This review environment returned URLError: Operation not permitted. This is not a measurement of either deployment host and does not prove their REST/artifact/GraphQL capabilities.

findings.suggested_fix: Choose an explicit read-only deploy route: an authorized operator pre-produces the exact-run A4 artifact and B3 verifies/consumes it, blocking if absent. Alternatively ask Q7 for scoped dispatch authority and budget the asynchronous run, polling and artifact retrieval. Verify actual REST, artifact redirect and provenance access on both deploy hosts. Test read-only credentials, absent/stale A4 artifacts, GraphQL null and timeout; missing provenance must remain blocked rather than becoming warning_only after blocking activation.

findings.location: §4 A+1; §5 B2 write set; §7; inherited r3 PR3/PR6 write sets
findings.claim: The repairs introduce executable enforcement without assigning all implementing paths. A+1 requires new trusted kiem-merge behavior, but inherited PR3/PR6 write sets omit packet_loop.py and its tests. B2 now requires the coordinator doctor to consume heartbeat state, but its write set contains only a new workflow, new ops script/tests and ci_dang_ky_test.py. The original R4-06 B1 dependency and registry omissions are fixed; this is a new manifestation of the same incomplete-scope class.

evidence.observed: PR3/PR6 planned write sets cover the classifier, ci.yml, cong_cu_test.py and ci_dang_ky_test.py, not the trusted merge consumer.
The existing doctor implementation is in launcher.py. r4 newly promises its heartbeat read, without assigning that path or declaring a manual runbook instead.
PR1 effective write set excludes these paths and even excludes the registry still held by PR0. Its frozen scope cannot absorb the new enforcement.

findings.suggested_fix: Assign the trusted consumer changes and tests to explicit future packet write sets, or add a successor that lands before activation; declare sensitive review and reconcile overlap before lease. If doctor means a manual coordination procedure, say so and name its runbook/delivery responsibility. Check every newly promised consumer against the final packet graph and write sets. Preserve PR1 spec/lease and do not silently extend a running executor.

findings.claim: 13,282 s is the median for eight shard jobs, not the total full-audit cost. Presenting two complete audit runs as approximately 2 × 13,282 job-seconds omits the registry and aggregation jobs. The cited number itself is correct; its use as the complete canary budget is incomplete.

evidence.observed: For the same 42 runs with eight successful shards, median shard sum=13,282 s, median full-run execution sum=15,205 s, median non-shard component=1,876.5 s. The quoted two-run subtotal is 26,564 s; twice the complete-run median is 30,410 s, before any A4/push-CI cost.

findings.suggested_fix: Label 26,564 s as the eight-shard subtotal, and budget registry/aggregation, A4 and the push observation separately. Use the complete-run estimate with its cohort and uncertainty rather than treating sums of component medians as an exact total. Recompute from the same run set after B1 without scheduling extra audits solely to improve the estimate.
